title: Desktop application, view model and widgets
objective: Finish the desktop's one-path work and make its structure match its documented layers: the defects fixed, the crop fully on the one draft driver with a declared angle stepper and a proxy stage, one start refusal, draft rounds that cost no extra frame, state owned by the seam that uses it, evidence that drives the shipped paths and the live-agent path, layers the repository check can enforce, and tests that prove each behaviour once.
context_summary: Waves 1 to 3 put the desktop's shared mechanisms on one path: one pure draft state machine behind one gesture slot and one start refusal, the crop on the one draft driver with a declared angle stepper and a proxy input stage at Fit, `draft.begin`, `draft.cancel` and `draft.reapply` answered synchronously, the armed brush as view state, one frame presenter, an idle loop that is asleep, a descriptor-driven control path with no module names in production UI code, and no stack or preview job kept between messages (the `desktop-keeps-no-stack` and `desktop-keeps-no-preview-job` repository rows). tasks.description: Make a double-click on the crop angle's rail reset the angle to 0 and send the change, instead of only rewriting the text box.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix.

`view/tools_panel.rs`'s `angle_stepper` wires the rail's reset to `Message::Crop(CropMessage::AngleText("0".into()))`, and `app/crop.rs`'s `CropMessage::AngleText` handler only assigns `self.crop_angle = text`; the draft, the rail and the canvas keep the pressed angle after the reset runs.

Every generic slider's double-click reset (`ResetField`) sets the field's default value and sends it as a real change; the crop angle is the one stepper that does not, because it predates the generic control path. No test or capture covers a double-click on the crop rail today.

The fix here is behavioural only: send the same change `NudgeAngle` sends. Removing the angle's separate model and messages once it is declared as a generic stepper is separate, later work in this plan.

tasks.description: Report a truncated diagnostics log: count events dropped past the cap, write one truncation record at finish, and fail an evidence run whose log was truncated.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix.

`diagnostics.rs`'s background writer keeps `Record::Event(value) if count < 4096 && !failed`; every event past the cap falls into the catch-all arm and is dropped with no record at all. `finish()` already returns `false` on a write or flush failure, but a truncated run still returns `true`.

A drag logs 4-5 diagnostic events per input; a recorded burst run reached 1,756 events for 360 inputs, so a `--data-root` session stops logging after roughly 850 drag inputs. An evidence run near the cap would silently lose the `round_trip_ms` records `editor-latency` reads, with nothing saying so.
Keep the cap; only make the drop loud. `finish()` failing on truncation is what lets evidence treat it exactly like the write failure it already handles.

tasks.description: Refuse Undo, Redo and Restore while a draft is open, through the one refusal rule, with the reason in the status bar.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix.

Owner decision (2026-09-26): Undo, Redo and Restore are refused while a draft is open, with the reason in the status bar, matching every other discrete commit (`app/actions.rs`'s `gesture_refusal` check before a mask command or a preset apply).

Today Cmd+Z is always mapped in `app/keymap.rs`; `app/sync.rs`'s `command()`, which every discrete commit calls, refuses only on `self.busy`; and `state/title.rs`'s `derive()` computes `can_undo`/`can_redo` from `editable` (state open, `can_edit()`, not busy) with no draft check, so the title bar shows Undo and Redo enabled during a draft.

Committing Undo, Redo or Restore over an open draft marks this client's own draft conflicted today, and `state/canvas.rs` reports it with one of three near-identical sentences ("Another client committed revision N while your slider draft was open", naming a mask gesture or a crop draft the same way) that is untrue: no other client committed anything. The user guide documents this as intended today ("another client, or your own Undo, Redo or Restore" marks the draft "Changed elsewhere"), so it needs updating along with the design.

Refuse at the UI entry points that call `command()` for Undo, Redo and Restore, not inside `command()` itself, since evidence's `api` step also goes through `command()` and must keep being able to exercise them directly for other checks.

tasks.description: Drive sliders in evidence and tests through the widgets' own messages and delete the evidence-only slider messages and the dead cancel message.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation.

`ControlMessage::SliderMoved` and `SliderReleased` (`app/message.rs`, handled in `app/controls.rs`) are sent only by the evidence driver (`app/evidence.rs`) and by tests; the slider widget itself sends `Fraction` and `Released`, wired in `view/tools_panel.rs`. `CancelEdit` is sent by no widget at all, only by tests.

The two paths disagree. On a non-drafting slider, `SliderMoved` writes a physical value into the field and marks it dragging without the `editable()` check `control_value` makes for `Fraction`, and without the fine-step snap `NumberSpec::at_fraction` applies; on a drafting one it reaches the gesture through `Editor::slider_moved` (`app/slider.rs`). `SliderReleased` releases an open slider gesture whichever control it belongs to, while `Released` releases only the control that is drafting. So the evidence steps and the slider tests prove a path the shipped widget never takes.

Evidence sends `SliderMoved` from three paths, `slider_step`, `double_click_step`'s first press and the paced `slider_paced_tick`, and `end_slider_gesture` sends `SliderReleased`; all of them convert. The generated-controls step already drives the widget path: `ControlsStep::Slider` sends `Fraction` and ends through `finish_generated_gesture`. Merge the `slider` step into it or build the conversion on it rather than write another driver; `Step::Key` (`key_step`), which replays keys through the real keymap, is the same precedent for keys.

`NumberSpec::at_fraction` (`state/number.rs`) maps a fraction to a value and has no inverse; add one. `at_fraction` spans the soft range and snaps to `fine_step`, so a scripted value outside the soft range or off the fine grid cannot round-trip, and the round-trip test names every such value. Give tests a `slide()` helper over the same messages.

The scripted values include `set-raw` Temperature drags in kelvin (the raw-panel smoke's 3500 K and 2500 K), double-clicks on `set-raw` Temperature and Tint and on `set-basic` Exposure, the basic smoke's JPEG Temperature drag, and `editor-latency`'s bursts on `set-raw` Temperature and Tint. A variant's field is keyed by its providing module (`set-raw.temperature`, seeded in `state/fields.rs`), so each value converts through its provider's `NumberSpec`.

Delete `SliderMoved`, `SliderReleased`, `Editor::slider_moved` and `CancelEdit` once nothing sends them, and add a `check-repository` rule that refuses a control message only evidence or a test constructs, so a future evidence-only message fails the same way. The check's existing `holds_whole_token` and `production_lines` helpers already answer both halves of that question.

tasks.description: Put the crop fully on the one draft driver: the shared commit, cancel and reapply messages, one refusal behind Apply, one conflict notice, a frame opened from the recipe rows with no change queue, and the crop's values and geometry taken from the core.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation.

Crop already runs on the core `draft.*` lifecycle, but keeps its own `CropMessage::{Apply, Cancel, Reapply}` beside the shared `DraftMessage::{Commit, Cancel, Reapply}`, which `app/gesture.rs`'s `release_refusal` already routes crop through via `crop_refusal`. It also keeps its own Enter/Escape branch in `app/keymap.rs`, two extra `NoticeAction` variants and a `mask: bool` flag on the draft bar, and three near-identical "Changed elsewhere" notices in `state/canvas.rs` that differ only by naming a slider draft, a mask gesture or a crop draft.

Whether Apply can run is decided in four places with three wordings: `state/tools.rs`'s `can_apply` (`enabled && !gesture_conflicted`, no wording); two copies of `apply_reason` in `state/canvas.rs`'s draft bar, one for a mask gesture and one for the crop draft, identical but for one word (conflicted, preview or busy); and `app/crop.rs`'s `crop_refusal` (busy, preview, conflicted, plus the output error, in other sentences). The view-model copies leave out the output check the app itself makes, so the button can read enabled while the app would refuse the request.

The start waits for a truncated, full-resolution render to learn a size every `recipe.describe` row already reports as `input_stage`; that produces a pending state, `app/crop.rs`'s 32-deep `QUEUED_CHANGES` with rail coalescing, "prospective" angle text parsed back in both `app/crop.rs` and `state/tools.rs`, and currency checks. Open the frame synchronously instead, from an existing crop's row (`input_stage` and `values`) or, for a new crop, the row at the insertion index; add an `output_stage` to `RecipeDescription` for the append case, since it does not exist there today.

The start also re-derives geometry the core already reports: `app/crop.rs`'s `orientation_ahead` parses `ORIENTATION_EFFECT` payloads and folds them on the desktop, although the develop-workspace design states "the desktop folds no geometry itself"; `crop_draft.rs` re-implements the core's own `refit` inline in `rebase` instead of calling it; and the crop aspect vocabulary is spelled twice (`crop/module.rs`'s presets and `crop_draft.rs`'s `parse_ratio`), where "free" means a different thing in each. Committed values are parsed too: `app/crop.rs`'s `committed_crop_angle` deserializes the current entry's crop layer into a `CropPayload` (the angle text's submit and reset short-circuits and `seed_idle_angle` call it), and `state/tools.rs`'s `committed_crop` deserializes the describe row's `values` into one to work out the angle and aspect. Read committed values and the orientation ahead of a row from `recipe.describe` instead of parsing payloads.

Folding the crop's keymap branch into the shared draft branch keeps the keymap's rules: an open Export menu's Escape still closes the menu before any draft hears it (a keymap test covers it); Escape from a pick taken on a mask still returns to Mask mode through `KeyContext::leave_to`; and Space and Option (`CropMessage::Space`, `CropMessage::Option`) stay crop-only.

Owner decision (2026-09-26): a crop draft opens before the stage's pixels arrive, so the section is live at once and the canvas shows the frame once the stage renders — delivered here; showing the input stage itself from a proxy at Fit is separate, later work in this plan. The owner also decided that `CropMessage::Cancel` on a draft that is still starting cancels it outright rather than being silently ignored as it is today; record that as the intended behaviour in the develop-workspace design, since it is more honest than doing nothing.

tasks.description: Declare the crop angle's step and fine step on its parameter and render it as the generic stepper control, deleting the crop's own angle model, messages and constants.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation.

The crop angle is a second, hand-built stepper beside the generic one: `state/tools.rs`'s `CropSectionModel` angle fields and `AngleRailModel`; `view/tools_panel.rs`'s `angle_stepper`, with its own Shift-x10/Option-divide-10 handling, and `angle_reset`; `app/crop.rs`'s `rail_angle` plus six angle-only messages (`AngleText`, `SubmitAngle`, `AngleRail`, `AngleRailReleased`, `NudgeAngle`, `ResetAngle`); and `crop_draft.rs`'s `ANGLE_STEP` (0.5) and `ANGLE_RAIL_STEP` (0.05).

The core's angle parameter (`modules/crop/module.rs`'s `angle_parameter`) declares no `step` or `fine_step`, although `ParameterDescriptor` already has both fields with builder methods used elsewhere, and `state/number.rs`'s `NumberSpec` already derives a rail step, nudge amounts, decimals and the reset value from whatever a parameter declares.

Declare `step: 0.5` and `fine_step: 0.05` on the angle parameter so agents can read the steps from the schema, then render the angle through the same generic stepper control every other numeric parameter uses, routing its field messages to the crop driver's frame action.

A double-click on the angle's rail sends its own `CropMessage::ResetAngle` (built by `view::tools_panel::angle_reset`), which `app/crop.rs` handles as its own case and short-circuits when the committed angle is already 0. This task deletes `ResetAngle`, `angle_reset` and that special case: the rail's double-click sends the generic `ControlMessage::ResetField`, whose `reset_field` (`app/slider.rs`) resets the field to its declared default and sends it, and `a_double_click_on_the_angle_rail_resets_the_angle_as_one_change` is ported to that message.

tasks.description: Answer "may this start" with one refusal function for every start site, and always write its reason to the status bar.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation.

The one-draft rule is one function, `app/gesture.rs`'s `gesture_refusal`, and its `Starting` enum already names every start (slider, mask, mask command, crop, mode, pick, gallery, compare, preset, action, history, refit). The busy and editability halves are re-written per call site with different wording: `app/slider.rs`'s `slider_refusal` and `app/masks.rs` say "Return to the current state before editing"; `app/pointer.rs` says "...before picking from the photograph" in its refusal but "...before editing" on a pick's commit; `app/crop.rs`'s `crop_refusal` says "A request is already in flight" and "Return to the current state before applying a crop"; `app/pointer.rs`, `app/masks.rs` and `app/presets.rs` say "Waiting for the last request".

Some sites fail silently: `crop_start` returns `Task::none()` on busy or a previewed entry with no status; `app/controls.rs`'s `Submit`, `control_value`, the colour picker's change and the curve's points change each return `Task::none()` when `!self.editable()`; and `app/slider.rs`'s `reset_field` drops a refused reset through `reset.filter(|_| self.editable())`. The developer gallery replaces the refusal's own text with a generic one of its own.

Extend `Starting` and `gesture_refusal` with the busy and editability halves, so one call answers "may this start"; every start site calls it and always writes the returned reason to the status bar, and no start site returns silently. Each `Starting` variant declares which halves apply. `Refit` takes the one-draft rule alone: `app/preview.rs`'s `refit_proxy` and `proxy_refit_deferred` and `app/masks.rs`'s overlay read `gesture_refusal(Starting::Refit).is_some()` as a flag, and a refit must still run while a request is in flight or a history entry is previewed. `History` never takes the editability half, since Restore runs from a previewed entry. `Slider` takes the one-draft rule and editability but not busy, as `slider_refusal` does today; `Crop`, `Mask`, `Pick`, `Action` and `MaskCommand` take all three, as their sites check today; `Mode`, `Gallery`, `Compare` and `Preset` keep the halves their sites check today, stated on the variant.

Export has its own refusals: `app/export.rs`'s `export_start` words busy as "Waiting for the last request" beside a running export and an open dialog, and `state/title.rs`'s `can_export` restates them for the menu. Route export's busy half through the one refusal with the one-draft rule stated as not applying, since export writes the displayed entry, which an open draft does not change; `can_export` reads the same answer.

Canvas-mode shortcuts, W among them, reach `ViewMessage::SetMode` (`app/view_state.rs`), which already refuses through `gesture_refusal(Starting::Mode)` and writes the reason; they need no start site of their own.

tasks.description: Compute visible curve controls, editability and group resets once in the view model and read them from there, instead of re-deriving them in the app.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation.

`app/controls.rs`'s `request_visible_curve_samples` runs from `app/mod.rs`'s update before `rederive`, re-derives which curve controls are on screen and gets it wrong: its `== Some(false)` check on the expanded-sections map ignores a module's declared `collapsed` default, so a curve declared collapsed like other sections would still be sampled while hidden; it also ignores `layout: tabs` (a curve in a hidden tab still counts as visible) and developer filtering, and it allocates the declared-curve list on every message.

It also skips the source-kind rules the view model applies to every section: `state/tools.rs` drops a section whose module does not apply to the photo's source kind (`applies`) and resolves each control to the module that provides it for that kind and target (`resolved`, `providers`), while `request_visible_curve_samples` walks every available module's declared controls with neither.

`editable` is computed four times with different shapes: a boolean in `app/mod.rs`'s `editable()`, the same boolean logic again in `state/title.rs`'s `derive` and `state/canvas.rs`'s `derive`, and a fourth, differently-worded version in `state/tools.rs`'s `disabled_reason`. tasks.description: Run `draft.begin`, `draft.cancel` and `draft.reapply` synchronously on the desktop thread, like `draft.set`, keeping only `draft.commit` as an owner task.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed.
Owner decision (2026-09-26): `draft.begin`, `draft.cancel` and `draft.reapply` run synchronously on the desktop thread like `draft.set`, proven by a press-to-first-frame measurement.

`draft.set` is already synchronous because every runtime hop costs about one displayed frame on the M4 at 120 Hz (performance rule 12, measured). `draft_begin_task` and the cancel and reapply tasks (`app/tasks.rs`) are still owner tasks, although the core implements all three as session-only operations behind `crates/luxforge-core/src/api/methods.rs`'s `draft.begin`/`draft.cancel`/`draft.reapply` handlers, none of which writes the catalog. So the first move of every slider, mask and crop gesture waits one avoidable hop for `Begun` before any `draft.set` can go.

The asynchrony is also why most of the driver's race handling exists: `app/draft.rs`'s `Round` enum tracks Begin, Reapply and Cancel rounds that would not exist if those calls were synchronous; `Gesture::Closing` (`app/gesture.rs`) and its "still opening"/"still closing" refusals exist only to block a new gesture while an old begin or cancel is in flight; and four of the seven draft races the mask work found (Apply before begin answers, a late begin adopted by a newer gesture, a late failed reapply, Discard adopting a session that still holds the draft) become impossible by construction once nothing is left in flight to race.

`CoreDraft` keeps only the `Set` and `Commit` rounds after this change; `Round::{Begin,Reapply,Cancel}`, `Gesture::Closing` and the three task wrappers and their message variants (`DraftMessage::{Begun,Reapplied,Cancelled}`) are deleted along with the race tests that exist only to prove states that no longer occur; name each deleted race test with why its race is now structurally impossible.

The develop-workspace design's message-flow section documents today's asynchronous shape ("the other four are owner tasks whose answers come back as one `Message::Draft` family"); it needs updating to describe the synchronous begin, cancel and reapply, leaving only commit as an owner task.

tasks.description: Hold an armed brush as view state and open its core draft at the press, so no empty draft exists between strokes.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed.

After each stroke commits, the desktop opens an empty `mask.add-stroke` draft immediately so the next press can call `draft.set` at once. That empty draft needs handling everywhere: every other gesture must take it over (`app/gesture.rs`'s `claim_slot`), every mask command must put it down first (`disarm`), release must refuse it, and a commit made elsewhere while it is open rebases it silently (`rebase_armed_brush`) instead of raising the usual conflict notice. That is roughly 60 lines of special-casing across `app/gesture.rs`, `app/masks.rs`, `app/slider.rs`, `app/crop.rs` and `app/tasks.rs`.

It also leaks into the API: `session.state` shows an open `mask.add-stroke` draft with no fields while a person merely holds the brush with nothing painted, and an agent's own commit conflicts a draft that represents nothing yet.

Make "armed" pure desktop view state (the brush in hand and its target component, no core draft). Open the core draft at the press with a synchronous `draft.begin`, the same synchronous treatment this plan gives every other draft round, immediately followed by the first `draft.set` in the same update. Delete the armed branches of `gesture_refusal`, `claim_slot`, `disarm`, `rebase_armed_brush` and the displaced-draft cancel in the begin path.

tasks.description: Show a crop draft's input stage at Fit from a proxy phase, with the exact stage only at a percentage zoom.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed.
Owner decision (2026-09-26): a crop draft at Fit shows its input stage at display resolution from the proxy, with the exact stage only at a percentage zoom.

Opening a crop draft today renders every pixel-stage layer before the crop at full resolution with no proxy phase at all, because `crates/luxforge-core/src/editor/evaluate.rs`'s preview-job planning filters the proxy whenever a truncated layer count is set. The whole frame is then uploaded into a texture: 230 MiB at 60 MP, 152 MiB for the X100VI, 92 MiB at 24 MP, held beside the photograph's own texture for the whole draft (`luxforge-ui/src/photo_surface.rs`). The frame cannot open until that render ends, recorded at about 3.9 s with all three Presence fields at 60 MP and about 0.36 s with a full Basic layer at 60 MP.

The stage is also the one display path the photograph's own proxy-then-exact job does not follow, and it is drawn at roughly a quarter size at Fit through a bilinear sampler with `mip_level_count: 1`, so fine texture is suspected to alias while cropping.

Give a truncated preview job a proxy phase whenever the desktop asks for bounds: plan the prefix's own proxy (the prefix before the crop holds no crop, so this is the proxy stage itself), present it at Fit, and let the exact phase follow only when a percentage zoom needs it, exactly as the photograph already behaves. The stage never feeds a commit, a sample or an analysis, so committed bytes are unaffected either way.

tasks.description: Measure what deriving every workspace region on every message costs, and remove the per-region keys if it stays under about 0.2 ms; otherwise key only the heavy region, on one value.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure.
Owner decision (2026-09-26): the per-region derivation keys are removed if the logged derivation stays under about 0.2 ms per message; otherwise only the heavy region is keyed, on one value.

The machinery is four layers deep and was added with no measurement: `Tracked` stamps on 15 `Editor` inputs (`state/tracked.rs`) plus a session stamp (`Built::session_stamp`, which deep-compares the whole `ClientSession`, an open draft's fields included, on every message and clones it when it changes); `state/mod.rs`'s `Stamps` and `Built` with eight hand-listed region keys (title, panel, canvas, masks, tools, histogram, status, palette) over the 77-field `Inputs`; per-section digests in `state/tools.rs` (`digest`, which on every tools refresh formats `module.availability` with `{:?}`, serializes each bound layer's payload to JSON, and for the crop builds `draft_digest`'s string, re-reading the committed crop and its aspect presets); and the debug-only `Workspace::check_kept` re-derivation that catches a key missing an input.

The per-input cost recorded before this machinery existed put the desktop's update, derivation and view under 0.15 ms together (the performance spec's "Instant previews: proxy phase, hop rule and the surface primitive"); the commit that added the keys did not re-measure, and nothing outside tests reads `SectionModel.version`. `view()` still rebuilds every widget of every section on every message regardless of the keys, so the machinery optimizes the cheaper half of the budget. While a draft is open the canvas region already re-derives on every message (`drafting_key`), with the tools region under a crop draft and the masks region under a mask draft, preview polls and timer ticks included.

How to measure with today's tools. `Editor::update_inner` (`app/mod.rs`) records `LoopTiming::last_rederive_ms` around `rederive` (with `request_capability_loads`, its second `rederive` when a capability section first loads, and `request_visible_curve_samples` inside the timed span), and `Editor::view` records `last_view_ms`. Nothing summarizes them: they reach the log only in each `slider_draft_preview` event's `detail.loop` object (`Editor::set_previewed`, `app/gesture.rs`), one sample per drafted input, taken from the update before that event's own. Build a release binary whose `Built::refresh` treats every key as moved (a temporary local change; `check_kept` is debug-only and does not run in it) and keep it beside an unchanged release build. Run `editor-latency --mode drag` (30 inputs by default) on the generated 24 MP and 60 MP JPEGs with `--binary` naming each build, back to back and then in reverse order, plus a `--mask` run so the masks region holds a bound mask. Read `detail.loop.last_rederive_ms` and `last_view_ms` from every `slider_draft_preview` in each run's `NEW_DIR/app/events.jsonl` and take p50 and p95; decide on the bypassed builds' p95. Mask and crop draft events carry no `loop` object, so the masked slider drag is the masked case this measures; `--mode burst` (360 paced inputs) adds samples if the drag's are too few to separate the branches.

If derivation stays under about 0.2 ms, delete `Tracked`, `Stamps`, `Built` and its keys, `check_kept`, the session stamp and the section digest and version, and derive every region on every message; keep the widget-level versions that key canvas caches (the curve's `curve_version` in `view/tools_panel.rs`) and the Performance section's own version, and build the palette's entries only while it is open (`palette::derive` filters every applicable module whether or not it is). If one region measures heavy instead, key only that region on one cheap value rather than keeping the framework.

The tests that prove the keys go with them or become behaviour checks: `a_refresh_builds_only_the_sections_whose_inputs_moved`, `a_field_change_re_derives_only_its_own_section`, `a_kept_section_that_differs_from_a_fresh_one_fails_a_debug_build` and `selecting_a_tab_rederives_only_its_own_section_and_changes_no_recipe` (`state/mod.rs`), `a_drag_re_derives_only_the_drafting_modules_section` (`app/slider_tests.rs`) and `a_message_that_changes_nothing_builds_no_section` (`app/view_state_tests.rs`). `cached_canvas_versions_track_picker_fractions_selection_and_drag_state` stays.

tasks.description: Give presentation its own owner, `preview::Presentation`, holding the presenter and the frame bookkeeping, with typed retained frames and one displayed-size rule.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure.

About 34 `Editor` fields hold presentation: the `presenter`; generations (`preview_generation`, `presented_generation`); content serials (`content_key`, `content_serial`, `pending_content`, `pending_intent`, `presented_content`, `analysis_content`, `raster_content`, `viewport_disabled_content`); retained frames (`proxy_frame`, the exact `raster`, `region_raster`) and their flags (`raster_approximate_white_balance`, `exact_render_ms`, `presented_proxy`, `presented_approximate_white_balance`); `analysis` and `incoming`; bounds (`pending_bounds`, `presented_bounds`, `refit_pending`, `proxy_declined`, `held_by_proxy`); `render_error`; entries (`presented_entry`, `requested_render_entry`, `rendered_entry`, `displayed_draft_revision`, `displayed_draft_id`); and the mask overlay's `mask_overlay_pending`, `pending_overlay` and `overlay_awaited`. `app/preview.rs` writes most of them, `gesture.rs`, `sync.rs`, `crop.rs` and `masks.rs` write some, and `overlay.rs`, `evidence.rs` and `snapshot.rs` read them.

`preview_ready` flattens the phase-typed preview result back into a 7-tuple; `Upload` (`app/tasks.rs`, named for an upload that no longer exists) re-adds the proxy flags so `present` can log them; `present_retained` (`app/preview.rs`) unpacks a `ProxyFrame` into seven locals to call `hand_retained`, which takes seven parameters under `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`.

The pure `state::histogram::displayed_size` exists, but its arguments for the current view (the zoom mapped to a `ZoomView`, `photo_surface` of the window and open panels, the scale factor and `view::canvas::FIT_INSET`) are assembled by hand at three sites: twice in `app/overlay.rs` and once in `Editor::proxy_bounds_for` (`app/preview.rs`). `requested_render_entry` and `rendered_entry` clone a whole `HistoryEntry` per refresh and per presented frame (`preview.rs`, `sync.rs`) only so `snapshot.rs` can report it.

The mask coverage grid arrives in its own message behind a proxy frame (`PhaseOutcome::Overlay`, taken up by `coverage_ready`) and beside the frame for an exact-only job or a region, but all three arrivals park it in `mask_overlay_pending` for `present_mask_overlay` (`app/masks.rs`), a post-dispatch step in `update_inner`, while the clipping overlay is already presented where it arrives.

Add `preview::Presentation`, owning the existing `Presenter` plus these fields, with `request(job) -> generation`, `take(result) -> Presented`, `zoom(wants_proxy)`, `withdraw()` and `surfaces()`. Retained frames become `enum Retained { Proxy(ProxyFrame), Exact(ExactFrame) }`, where `ExactFrame` gathers the exact raster and its flags, presented through one function; delete `Upload`. Write one method for the current view's displayed size and call it from the three sites. Present the coverage grid where each arrival takes it up, with no pending field or post-dispatch step. Keep the evidence stack summary on ids or a shared reference, not per-frame clones.

The crop draft's input stage stays with the crop gesture: its frames are `StageFrames` on the gesture (`app/crop.rs`, keeping no `PreviewJob`), shown by `present_crop_stage`, which returns a `Task`; `draft_generation` moves beside them in the seam split rather than onto `Presentation`. `Presentation::request` takes a `PreviewJob`, so keep `Presentation` in `app/preview.rs`, one of the files the `desktop-keeps-no-preview-job` repository row allows, or add its own file to that row's allowed list and test (`only_the_files_that_pass_a_preview_job_through_name_one_on_the_desktop`); it keeps no job once the queue has it.
The layering task's framework-free `layout.rs` takes `photo_surface` and the panel constants; whichever of the two lands second builds its displayed-size method on the other's.

This is presentation-only: the Presenter's own behaviour (versioned frames, cheap-cloned zoom hand-overs, adopting an exact phase behind a presented proxy without a texture write) is proven and unchanged; renders and presented bytes stay identical.

tasks.description: Have production code report typed evidence outcomes instead of steering the evidence driver, build diagnostic events only when a log exists, and keep evidence-only state inside the evidence driver.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure.

Evidence stays compiled into the shipped binary, because smoke runs the packaged binary; that is unchanged by this task. The cost is coupling: production seams call `settle_step` with evidence's own `Settle` categories at 49 sites across 12 files (`pointer.rs` 13, `crop.rs` 7, `preview.rs` 7, `gesture.rs` 6, `presets.rs` 4, `evidence.rs` 3, `view_state.rs` 3, `masks.rs` 2, and one each in `capabilities.rs`, `export.rs`, `overlay.rs` and `performance.rs`), so every seam has to know evidence's own vocabulary.

`Editor::event` (`app/mod.rs`) builds its JSON value, with the run id, build version and elapsed time, before it checks for a log sink; a normal drafted frame builds around five of these (a recorded burst run produced 360 `slider_draft_set`, 360 `slider_draft_preview`, 313 `preview_displayed` and 277 `preview_exact_cancelled` events for 360 inputs), all discarded when no log exists.

Replace paired `event`/`settle_step` calls with one typed outcome (for example a frame-presented event carrying its generation, proxy state and drain state, or a refusal carrying its reason) that the diagnostics log serializes and the evidence driver matches to whatever settle condition it is waiting on. Make `event` lazy: check for a sink, or take a closure, before building the value. Move evidence-only retention (clones kept only for the log or the captured state) into the evidence driver's own type, filled only when it is present; the presentation owner's entry clones are the largest, if that task has not already moved them.

The recorded-run mutation replay (`SMOKE_RECORDED=DIR cargo test -p xtask mutations -- --ignored`, over the `DIR/smoke-<scenario>/run` directories `verify` writes) must still fail each migrated scenario on its removed last step and on its changed first label, proving the settle conditions still discriminate once they are typed.

tasks.description: Match core controls directly instead of through the `Rendered` mirror, hold per-control local state in one map, and delete the dead-code allowances that hid unread fields.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure.

`state/tools.rs`'s `Rendered<'a>` copies core `Control` field for field, plus an `Unsupported` variant `classify` can never produce: `Control` (`luxforge-core/src/modules/descriptor.rs`) is not `#[non_exhaustive]` and deserializes with a `kind` tag and `deny_unknown_fields`, so an unknown kind cannot arrive at runtime. The fallback arm carries `#[allow(unreachable_patterns)]`, and `control_kind()` serializes a whole control to JSON to name that impossible case (and, once, a control whose providing module is not registered). `classify` is called at 17 sites across `state/tools.rs`, `state/fields.rs`, `state/masks.rs` and `state/presets.rs`, with about 70 `Rendered::` matches.

`ControlsUi` holds eight parallel maps keyed by (action, parameter[, index]) — curve channels, curve points, curve edits, curve samples, colour-picker open state, colour channels, colour hex text and the HSV picker cache — plus `group_expanded` and `selected_tab`, and the section digest scans every one of them for every action of every module on each refresh.

18 struct-level `#[allow(dead_code)]` markers sit in `state/tools.rs` (8), `state/masks.rs` (6) and `state/panel.rs` (4), mostly on view-model types that derive `Debug`/`PartialEq` (which would already satisfy rustc's own dead-field lint); at least one covered type is confirmed live from other call sites, so the allows read as a habit from when these structs were built out field by field rather than a still-needed suppression. `EnumControl.segmented` is written but never read, since the view matches on `style` instead.

tasks.description: Render the live-agent path in evidence: a scripted step that edits through a second client, with the event sync on in evidence runs, and move the "Changed elsewhere" frames onto it.
extra_context: Wave 5, tests.

Live agents editing alongside a person are a headline capability, and their changes reach the screen through one path: the owner wakes the desktop, a sync message fires, `events.since` answers, a refresh for another client's change runs, and the draft is marked conflicted. Evidence runs switch that path off (`Editor::subscription` in `app/mod.rs` adds `waker::events_subscription` only when no evidence is active, and `sync_when_wanted` in `app/sync.rs` returns early during an evidence run), so no rendered run shows another client's change arriving; it is covered only by unit tests (`app/sync_tests.rs`, `app/preview_failure_tests.rs`, `app/tasks.rs`).

Today the `basic` and `workspace` smokes' conflict frames (their `conflict` steps in `xtask/src/basic_smoke.rs` and `xtask/src/workspace_smoke.rs`) come from the desktop's own client committing through the evidence driver's `api_step`, and the captured notice (`state/canvas.rs`) says "Another client committed revision N while your … was open", which is not what happened. Other scenarios (`crop`, `export`, the mask acceptance) drive conflicts the same way and can follow once the step exists.

Add an `agent` evidence step (in `luxforge-evidence`) that sends through a second client registered on the same owner; enable the event subscription in evidence runs; settle the step on the sync's refresh reaching the screen. Move the conflict frames of the `basic` and `workspace` smokes onto this step.

Events already name their subject: each names the asset and revision it changed, and the desktop's sync refreshes only for the photo it has open, so the step can settle on the refresh for its own commit's revision.

tasks.description: Key the photo surface's GPU slots by a surface id carried in its primitive, so two surfaces can be on screen at once.
extra_context: Wave 6, roadmap groundwork.

Blocked: starts with the library milestone on the roadmap, whose virtualized browsing across many photos (a grid, filmstrip or side-by-side compare) is the first place a second photo surface would appear on screen at once.

Iced keeps one rendering pipeline per primitive type, and `luxforge-ui/src/photo_surface.rs`'s `PhotoPipeline` holds one set of slots for the whole application: four photo slots (`slots`), two viewport-region sets (`regions`) and the retirement accounting behind the overlap ceiling. Two photo surfaces drawn in the same frame today would overwrite each other's textures and uniforms, both would show whichever was prepared last, and both would re-upload every frame instead of only on a version change.

Key the pipeline's slots by a surface id carried in the primitive, and release a surface's slots by that id when it goes away. Library thumbnails do not need this: they can use Iced's own image widget with handles built outside `view()`, since the extra hop matters little for a grid of small images.

The owner's provisional overlap ceiling (one current and one retiring full-photo allocation of at most 512 MiB each plus two region sets of at most 32 MiB each, 1088 MiB in all) is one photo-texture budget shared by every photo surface (docs/decisions.md, "Plan refresh", 2026-09-28): a second surface draws from it, for example at display resolution, rather than doubling it, and the retirement accounting counts every surface's slots against it.
